cards.#1: The Blooming Grounds artwork is knitted into the body of this polo rather than printed on top of it — sky, treeline, creek and fairway, rendered as a full custom jacquard in one hundred per cent acrylic. A knit rib collar, three matte pearl buttons and a Kookaburra patch on the left sleeve finish it. Sizes run S to XXXL, and the whole drop is built around it.
cards.#2: This is the hand-drawn version: 250gsm cotton jersey on an oversized block, with the Hedge Script printed small at the chest and the full-colour Blooming Grounds scene running across the back. At fifty dollars it is the cheapest way into the collaboration, and the artwork gets more room here than it does anywhere else.
cards.#3: Lightweight poly-cotton seersucker is cut here with a wide camp collar, five centre-front buttons and a self-lined back yoke, with tiny embroidered golfers mid-swing scattered across it. Walker say to size up for a relaxed fit and pitch it as a shirt for a warm spring afternoon on a verandah, which in Austin covers roughly nine months of the year.
cards.#4: Walker builds the Featherlite block in a cotton-poly-elastane pique, and this one gets a custom striped ribbed collar, contrast sleeve bands and a three-button placket. It is the most conventionally golf-looking piece in the collaboration, and the one that will get the most wear.
cards.#5: The hood runs 400gsm brushed fleece with a soft interior, a kangaroo pouch sized for a scorecard and a glove, and chunky ribbed cuffs and hem. The Hedge Script is chain-stitched at the chest and the Kookaburra sits on the left sleeve. It is built for a cold walk from the carpark, which makes it a December garment in Austin rather than an August one.
cards.#6: Soft cotton twill sits on a mid box-cap block in navy, with contrast Star White stitching through the crown and brim. A large 14cm front panel carries the Hedge Script embroidery, the Kookaburra sits on the back right, and it closes with a rear snapback. The contrast stitching is what stops a navy cap from disappearing into every other navy cap, and it is fifty dollars in one size.
cards.#7: One hundred per cent acrylic goes into a custom stripe knit here, with a fine contrast stripe running through the body and knit collar, cuffs and hem. Three matte buttons close the placket. Gold Label is Walker’s premium line, and this is its plainest and best piece.
cards.#8: The same classic-fit block comes in a lightweight acrylic ombre knit that graduates from pale to charcoal down the body, and the placket is a quarter-zip rather than buttons. The gradient is knitted rather than dyed, which is why it reads as a fade instead of a wash.
cards.#9: A plaid twill body carries a satin quilted lining, a 16-wale corduroy collar and a full-length YKK antique brass zip. At $180 it is the most expensive piece in the Gold Label run, and it looks the least like golf clothing of anything Walker make.
cards.#10: A wool-blend knit with a brushed finish takes a fisherman-style ribbed collar and cuffs. Walker run it in Indigo and Almond, and the Indigo is the better of the two. It is a sweater you would keep on for the drive home without thinking about it.
cards.#11: An acrylic-blend yarn is worked into a textured three-stripe knit on a crew block, again with the fisherman collar. Chocolate with a red and cream stripe is the most seventies thing Walker make, and it reads as a sweater first and golf second.
cards.#12: Walker pitch their Heritage line as golf before the game went global, and the Crest is the hero of it: a classic rugby block with a cut-and-sew stripe panel running through the body and sleeves, finished with a white cotton-twill woven collar. The collar is the part that keeps it on the right side of costume.
cards.#13: Par-Tec is Walker’s technical line for 2026: lightweight, moisture-wicking, and built for airflow rather than for looks. Most technical polos read as gym kit on a golf course, and the Knockout V in Maple at $119 is the one in the range that avoids that.
cards.#14: Full-grain leather is lined with velvet and carries an embroidered “Dancing Kooka” pattern across the whole cover rather than a patch on one face. Eighty-nine dollars is real money for a driver headcover, and the all-over embroidery is where it goes. The forest and white reads as club colours rather than as a cartoon.
cards.#15: Nine-wale cotton corduroy is cut on the mid-profile box block, with contrast top-stitching on the peak and a snapback closure. The embroidered Kooka patch sits on the front and a Bounce logo on the right side. Walker run the corduroy caps in a rotating set of colours, and the red is the one to have at $49.

kickers.1: Two pieces carry the Blooming Grounds illustration, a course scene of trees, a creek and a green. On the polo it is knitted into the body rather than printed on top, which is a different and more expensive way to do it.
kickers.2: The other four run on Walker’s Hedge Script, a chain-stitched wordmark with a tiny golfer teeing off out of the W, plus the Kookaburra patch that turns up somewhere on almost everything they make.
kickers.3: Blooming Grounds is six pieces out of a much bigger catalogue, and the rest of it is where Walker actually live. Gold Label is the premium end and runs to knits. Heritage is the clubhouse throwback, Par-Tec is the technical line, and Kooka Classics is the core, named for the kookaburra.
kickers.4: Six pieces run one hemisphere out of step with Austin. The seersucker shirt and the Featherlite polo work here now; the fleece hood and the twill jacket are December buys.
